short: The Praetorian Guard sold the imperial throne to the highest bidder after murdering the previous emperor.
full:
After the Praetorian Guard murdered Pertinax on 28 March 193, having grown resentful of his attempts at discipline, the guard announced that the throne would go to whoever paid them the most. Titus Flavius Sulpicianus, Pertinax's father-in-law, bid from inside the Praetorian camp while Didius Julianus bid from outside its walls; the price rose in stages until Julianus offered 25,000 sesterces per soldier, and the guard proclaimed him emperor that same day.

The spectacle disgusted the Senate and the wider public, and the provincial armies refused to recognise a throne bought rather than earned. Septimius Severus, commanding the legions in Pannonia, marched on Rome within weeks; Julianus was abandoned by the guard that had sold him the office and was executed on 1 June 193, after a reign of 66 days. The episode became the standing example of Praetorian power over the principate at its most naked.
